module.summary: Turn a probability model into an objective for observed data.

stages.title: Building likelihoods: research guide
stages.html:
Building likelihoods

Turn a probability model into an objective for observed data.

A likelihood is the joint density or mass evaluated at the data and viewed as a function of parameters; support and factorization are part of the model.

Workflow. Build the joint density or mass as a function of parameters for observed data.

Diagnostic: Inspect support, independence factorization, and constants. The main failure to avoid is an objective that is not the model's likelihood.

stages.title: Building likelihoods: worked Python model
stages.note: Run the reproducible example, then change one assumption and compare the output.
stages.code:
import numpy as np
y = np.array([1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1])
grid = np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, 181)
loglike = np.array([(y*np.log(p) + (1-y)*np.log(1-p)).sum() for p in grid])
p_hat = grid[np.argmax(loglike)]
print(f"Grid MLE: {p_hat:.3f}")
print(f"Sample mean: {y.mean():.3f}")

stages.title: Score equations: model decision
stages.note: A team is about to report results without checking gradient magnitude and parameter constraints.

steps.prompt: What is the best next action?
choices: Differentiate the log-likelihood and interpret zero score at an interior optimum.
Increase decimal precision and report immediately.
Drop observations until the preferred coefficient appears.
steps.explain: The defensible workflow is to differentiate the log-likelihood and interpret zero score at an interior optimum.

steps.prompt: Which risk should the final report address explicitly?
choices: Only whether the sample mean is positive.
declaring convergence while the score remains large
Whether every coefficient has the same sign.
steps.explain: The relevant failure mode is declaring convergence while the score remains large.
